mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by more than 0.25% over the next month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to turn negative due to tightened credit conditions.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the identified FEDFUNDS increase (p > 0.05) or the rate rise is <0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE above 7.0% predicts a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return as higher unemployment weakens consumer and business sentiment.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 7.0% in the current month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive or not significantly different from zero (p > 0.05) during the UNRATE >7.0% regime.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly GDP demand (GDPC1) grows faster than industrial production (INDPRO) by at least 2%, the S&P 5-day forward return is positive, reflecting excess demand for equities.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth rate > INDPRO growth rate by ≥2% in the current month
regime_hint: Economic expansion with outpacing demand growth
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) when the GDPC1/INDPRO growth gap is ≥2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 3% predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return as weak manufacturing signals softening demand.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >3% in the current month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative or the decline in INDPRO is ≤3%.

mechanism_narrative: During a 3-month decline in the CPIAUCSL inflation index below 2%, the S&P 20-day forward return tends to be positive as the market anticipates rate cuts.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by ≥1% over the next 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) when CPIAUCSL declines <1% or inflation remains above 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in employment (PAYEMS) exceeding 10,000 monthly suggests labor market strength that supports equity valuations, predicting a positive 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10,000 in the current month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not positive or the increase in PAYEMS is ≤10,000.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly retail sales (implied via HOUST) exceed 900K units for two consecutive months, the S&P 20-day forward return is expected to be positive reflecting optimism in consumer spending.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the identified high sales period.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both RSAFS (demand) and INDPRO (supply) by at least 5% in the same month predicts a negative S&P 5-day forward return due to market overreaction to supply-side weakness.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls by ≥5% and INDPRO falls by ≥5% in the current month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not negative or the decline in both series is <5%.
